subject: Why the 2026-10-28 capacity run (capacity-repeats-20261028T080352534437Z) was stopped by the host for critically low memory

host_configuration_measured_2026-10-28.wslconfig: none (%USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig absent) -> WSL default: guest MemTotal 7538 MiB, swap 2048 MiB, 32 vCPU
host_configuration_measured_2026-10-28.gpu: RTX 5070 Ti Laptop, 12227 MiB VRAM, ~0.9 GiB used idle
host_configuration_measured_2026-10-28.competing_workloads_idle: Windows available ~3.5-5.5 GiB with WSL idle; largest other processes: opencode (~1-2 GiB private), Brave (~2.5 GiB across processes), dwm (~1 GiB), Defender, Claude Code, Wispr Flow. Not project-owned; not terminated.

probe1_before_fix.evidence: probe1-before-fix.samples.jsonl (3 s samples) + run capacity-custom-20261028T113002785163Z (stage C, 4 feeds, 20 s warm-up + 90 s; diagnostic durations, not acceptance)
probe1_before_fix.vmmem_mib: 1051 before -> 4362 at +24 s -> 4551 at +231 s (still rising ~0.9 MiB/s)
probe1_before_fix.orchestrator_rss_mib: ~45 during the step; after the step, parsing one 86 MiB stage-B JSONL with the old read_jsonl() peaked at 443 MiB (orchestrator_parse_probe.py), and each file was parsed twice

measurements.drvfs_cache_check: writing 300 MiB to /mnt/c and reading the 557 MiB clip from WSL did not change guest Cached: the growth was not drvfs I/O

diagnosis: Primary, project-owned: scripts/deepstream.sh ran `docker run` with the daemon's default json-file log driver, so every AEGIS_FRAME_V1 stdout record (~4 KiB per frame at stages B-D, ~120 KiB/s per feed) was also written to /var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/<id>-json.log inside the WSL VM. That grew the guest page cache, and therefore the host's Vmmem, linearly for the whole run (~0.7 GiB per 13-min step at 4 feeds, ~1.7 GiB over a 30-min soak) without ever being read.

Contributing, host: four DeepStream containers need ~2.6-2.9 GiB of additional host memory (Vmmem), and competing non-project applications leave only ~3.5-4 GiB available before a step starts, so steady state sits at ~1.3 GiB available; the extra linear growth above pushed the host to the critical threshold during stage B repeat 2 (the 6th step of the session).

Contributing, orchestrator: read_jsonl() loaded whole files (86 MiB text -> ~400 MiB of decoded dicts), run_containers() parsed each file a second time only to read its first record, and the old _has_covered() tail read assumed a record fits in 4 KiB. Transient (released after each feed), but it peaked exactly at the end of a step when Vmmem had not yet shrunk.
fixes: scripts/deepstream.sh: --log-driver none (attached docker run still streams stdout to the backend; nothing in the project uses docker logs). Verified by probe2: guest cache and Vmmem flat.

scripts/benchmark/run_capacity.py: streaming per-line aggregation keeping only timing scalars in compact arrays; first/last record readers that never parse the whole file and handle records larger than any fixed buffer; bounded resource sample buffers streamed to disk; a predeclared resource guard (host available/commit, WSL MemAvailable, GPU temperature) and a per-step headroom preflight that end the run as INTERRUPTED with cleanup instead of letting the host kill it.
not_done_deliberately: No change to .wslconfig, pagefile, WSL memory size, or other applications; no guest drop_caches during measurement.
